option: (a) A country field and the store's address, set by the seller
needs: Nothing particular in any market.
note: A reading: the field holds Yemen whichever of its two areas the store is in (YK-12); what differs by area is S02-D3's and S02-D7's.

option: (b) A business entity holds it: a legal entity with its own address, assignable to markets
needs: A legal business behind the store, a person trading alone or a company, with its country and address; to trade from a shop, an entry in the commercial register.
as_of: YE-B102, YE-B104, YE-B105, YE-B106: 1991 (effective); YE-F416: 1991-04-13 (effective, as amended); YE-B253: 2026-10-10 (captured); YE-B268: 2024-01-08; YE-B156 to YE-B158: 2010
note: The 1991 law bars trading in a shop to anyone not entered in the register of the shop's district (read as two facts: one entered may trade in a shop; one not entered may not; trading with no shop, such as online only, is not addressed). An individual merchant applies within 60 days of starting to trade, a company within 60 days of starting its activity (1991); a page the records place in the Houthis' area gives 30 days from founding or licensing (captured 2026-10-10), and the Sana'a ministry's register is electronic only (2024-01-08). The Minister may exempt small merchants the regulation defines. A seller's documents to consumers, electronic ones included, must show its name, address, phones and commercial register number (2010 regulation of Law 46 of 2008). The records hold no register rule for the government's area beyond the 1991 law, and nothing on whether one area's registration counts in the other (S-07's).

option: (c) The billing address the merchant pays the platform from
needs: A way to pay the platform's fees, issued in the seller's country, so that the billing address is there. An assumption, marked as one: the platform bills from outside the seller's country (where its company is based is S-03's, open), so the way to pay must reach foreign sites.
as_of: YE-D914, YE-D915, YE-D162: 2026-10-10 (issuers' pages, captured); YE-D103: 2025-06-15
note: Kuraimi's Pluto Debit Mastercard is offered for use 'inside Yemen or around the world', and MEPS's National Wallet card for paying on global shopping platforms (each issuer's own page). A 2025 article: paying foreign platforms in rials through some banks is limited to one or two wallets and not available in every governorate. Which provider Sharrwah bills through, and whether it takes these cards, is S-11's. Were the company based in the seller's country, a domestic way to pay would serve instead; that case is not tested here.

option: (d) A location set on a map or by hand
needs: Nothing particular in any market.

option: (e) The store's currency beside its address
needs: A store currency, read beside the address as the country's own.
note: The rial's one code covers two currency areas, old notes in the Houthis' north and new notes in the government's south and east (2026-10-10), at 533 rials to the dollar in Sana'a (old notes, 2026-10-08) and 1,562 buying in Aden (2026-10-10). Domestic sales must be paid in rials, yet the Saudi riyal dominates dealings in Aden and the government's areas, and some online stores price in dollars or only in Saudi riyals (S02-D7 (a)). A reading: a store's currency in Yemen may name neither its country nor its area.

option: (f) A seat setting beside the country (مقر المتجر)
needs: Nothing particular in any market.

option: (g) A country per storefront, shown as the store's
needs: Nothing particular in any market.

option: (a) Changed in place at any time
needs: Nothing particular in any market.

option: (b) Changed in place once conditions hold (financial services off, addresses in the entity's country, one individual entity per person and country)
needs: Nothing particular in any market: the conditions are the platform's own.

option: (c) No one changes it; a change makes a new entity or account
needs: A business entity in the new country, as S02-D1 (b).
note: For a move into Yemen, S02-D1 (b)'s facts.

option: (d) The platform changes it (staff, on request or under a contract)
needs: Nothing particular in any market.

option: Every option, (a) to (d)
needs: For the rules that differ by the seller's place to follow a move, the move must be a change of country.
evidence: YK-12 (YE-E1308, YE-E1289); YA-44 (YE-A005, YE-D423); YK-124 (YE-D521; corrections.md)
product_gap: A seller who moves between two such areas of one country changes the authorities and the currency area it answers to while its country stays the same. A move defined as a change of country doesn't catch it, so the checks a move runs would not run. The register's second pass takes the gap up in S02-D8, option (c).
note: A reading from these facts: a seller moving between Sana'a and Aden stays in Yemen but moves between two currency areas and between the two central banks' areas; payment providers from Sana'a are not authorised to operate in Aden without separate infrastructure in the South (2024-04-05; corrections.md: one direction only; read as two facts: without it they may not; that they may with it is not stated).

option: (a) The merchant's country (terms, the platform's payment service, other providers, fees, features)
needs: Every rule that follows the seller's place to be one per country.
evidence: YA-160 (YE-D012, YE-E785); YA-165 (YE-F352, YE-E795); YK-209 (YE-B102); YK-12 (YE-E1289, YE-E892, YE-D422, YE-D423, YE-E1308); YA-44 (YE-A005, YE-A088; YE-D435 and YE-D436 at place not stated, as corrections.md places them); YA-102 (YE-D113, YE-E193; corrections.md caution); YK-124 (YE-D520, YE-D521; corrections.md); YA-15 (YE-E1307, YE-C048); YA-03 (YE-B027, YE-E669); YA-25 (YE-D807, YE-E467, YE-E934); YA-26 (YE-D107); cases YC-116, YC-117, YC-119, YC-288, YC-101
product_gap: Where one country's areas answer to different authorities for payment services, the currency and the exchange rate, a rule keyed on the seller's country gives one answer for areas whose answers differ. The seller's area within the country, which the business record's address holds, may need to be a key beside the country. None of this decision's options keys on an area within a country (register.tsv); the register's second pass takes the gap up as S02-D8, and S02-D3 no longer closes it.
note: One per country in the records: the general sales tax, 5 percent of sales of goods and services; what a registered seller's invoice shows, the buyer's name, address and tax registration number among them; the 1991 commercial register law. Per area: two central banks, in Sana'a and Aden, whose decisions and policies on exchange companies conflict (2026-07-10); institutions operating nationwide answer to both (2024-04-05); the Sana'a bank licenses banking in its area (2024-05-31); the Aden bank issued rules for payment-service providers (2022-09-21), while on the Sana'a side non-banks were made eligible for e-rial services (corrections.md's caution: state the rule per area); the World Bank finds the two regions' payment frameworks similar, but Sana'a providers are not authorised in Aden without separate infrastructure in the South (2024-04-05; read as two facts, as S02-D2); each area has its own notes and central-bank rate (S02-D7). A reading: which providers a seller can use, and its starting currency, follow its area, not only its country. Changing (Q2's cases): each side barred the other's banks in May 2024 (YC-116, YC-117), and both agreed in July 2024 to cancel those decisions (partly reversed, 2026-02); Aden barred 12 wallets in June 2024 (YC-119, YC-288; 'licensed ones only', read as two facts: licensed wallets allowed, the 12 named barred), later reversed (2025-06-15); Aden provided in 2024 for withdrawing notes printed before 2016 (YC-101). No case varies YK-12 itself: one currency and one central bank for the whole country is a constant of the records.

option: (b) The store's country (services, the store's defaults, its currency, checkout fields, tax settings)
needs: As (a).
note: A reading: the store's address names a governorate or city, but this option keys on the country.

option: (c) The business's registered country
needs: A register in which the business is entered, and, as (a), every rule that follows the seller's place one per country.
evidence: As S02-D1 (b) for the register; as (a) for the rules.
note: The register exists (the 1991 law; the Sana'a ministry's electronic register): yes. The country of registration is Yemen in either area, so the rules that differ by area are as (a): no.

option: (d) A business entity
needs: As S02-D1 (b), and as (a).

option: (e) Every store alike
needs: Nothing particular in any market.

option: (f) The merchant's country for the defaults (starting currency, language)
needs: A starting currency and language for the country.
note: The country gives the rial, whose one code covers two currency areas; domestic sales must be paid in rials, yet the Saudi riyal dominates dealings in Aden and the government's areas (S02-D7 (a)). Language: nothing particular.

option: (a) Places: one or several countries, a region, a city
needs: Places a buyer's address names: the country, and within it a governorate, district or city.
as_of: YE-C138, YE-C266: 2026-10-10 (providers' pages, captured); YE-D049, YE-D050: 2025-09-08
note: Services name their reach by governorate and district: Jawali, the Republic in all its governorates; Yemen Wallet (Yemen Post), all districts; local companies ship between governorates, some routes with difficulty. A reading: these units exist as places an address can name.

option: (a) Places: a region that follows an area whose conditions differ
needs: For a market that follows one of the two currency areas, or one central bank's area, that area's bounds as places a buyer's address names.
what_would_show_it: A dated source listing the governorates and districts each authority holds, saying whether any is split between them, and how the bounds have moved.
note: The records name the currency areas by authority and direction ('the north', 'the south and east'), not by governorate, and hold no axis for who holds which place, so Q2 has no case of the bounds moving.

option: (b) A sales channel, a storefront, a point of sale, business customers, Salla Point, a market within a market
needs: Nothing particular in any market.

option: (c) Conditions a buyer matches: region, company location, point of sale, channel
needs: For a region condition, as (a); the other kinds need nothing particular in any market.
note: Countries, governorates and cities: yes, as (a); a region that follows an area whose conditions differ: unknown.

option: (d) Channel, point of sale or customer group as dimensions apart from markets
needs: Nothing particular in any market.

option: (a) One country per market
needs: Nothing particular in any market.

option: (b) A country, a region or a company location in more than one market, overlaps settled by the most specific settings
needs: For a market narrower than the country (one currency area) beside one for the whole country, the buyer's place within the country, as S02-D4 (a).

option: (c) A site or a locale in one market only
needs: Nothing particular in any market.

option: (d) Rules by kind (no web presence, domains or discounts in channel markets; one set of settings for online and in-store buyers of a region)
needs: Nothing particular in any market.

option: (e) A buyer placed by their country; the seller setting which customers may enter each market
needs: The buyer's country, from the address or location: nothing particular in any market.
note: A buyer's country doesn't say which of the two currency areas a buyer in Yemen is in; placing by area is (b)'s need.

option: (a) A value per market
needs: Nothing particular in any market.
evidence: YK-124 (YE-D521; corrections.md); YK-452 (YE-E082, YE-E083, YE-F086, YE-F087; corrections.md); YA-139 (YE-D050); YA-177 (YE-D606)
note: Facts that differ by area, for settings this decision lists: payment methods (Sana'a providers not authorised in Aden without separate infrastructure in the South; a community-written client of Kuraimi's E-Pay sets which currency zone's customers it accepts, old, new or all, which corrections.md says is not the provider's documentation); shipping (difficult between some governorates; the Houthi authorities treated their areas as an independent state, so that buying goods from them became like importing); the currency (S02-D7). A reading: a value per market holds these only where a market can follow an area (S02-D4 (a), unknown).

option: (b) Once for the whole store
needs: Nothing particular in any market.
note: A store set up this way holds one value for buyers in both currency areas; the facts that differ by area are (a)'s.

option: (c) A store value each market inherits and may override
needs: Nothing particular in any market.

option: (d) Narrower keys: a product's shipping and payment restrictions
needs: Nothing particular in any market.

option: (d) Narrower keys: checkout fields by the buyer's country (the address form)
needs: The fields of a delivery address in the buyer's country.
what_would_show_it: A source giving the fields a delivery address in Yemen uses (the postal operator's or a courier's address form, or a reference address dataset); Stage 1's records hold none.
note: What a registered seller's tax invoice shows of the buyer is held (name, address and tax registration number: YE-F352, 2002-05-25; YE-E795, 2022-01-01), under S02-D3 (a).

option: (a) A currency per market
needs: A currency for each market the store sells to in the country that its buyers there can pay in: the rial, in the notes of their currency area, or a foreign currency where the law allows it.
product_gap: S02-D9, two currency areas under one currency code, which no reference meets: one currency code can cover two currency areas of one country, with notes one area doesn't accept and exchange rates about three to one apart. A currency held by its code, a rate held per currency, and an amount stored with its code alone can't tell the areas apart; and a market drawn for an area within a country inherits its parent's currency (register.tsv, S02-D9 (b)), so no reference sells the two areas under one code at two rates.
note: Two currency areas under one code (2026-10-10): old notes in the Houthis' north, where the Sana'a bank banned the Aden bank's new notes in January 2020, and new notes in the government's south and east, where all notes were legal tender (2020-02-26) and Aden provided in 2024 for withdrawing notes printed before 2016 (YC-101: which notes an area accepts changes). 'Two currencies are in circulation, though only one is accepted across the country' (2024-04-05; read as two facts: one is accepted everywhere, the other is not). Domestic sales must be paid in rials (Council of Ministers' decision 13 of 2025; the government's enforcement, 2026-04-24; a seller may not require a foreign currency, 2010), yet the Saudi riyal dominates dealings in Aden and the government's areas (2025-10-28) and is widely used (2025-12-26), and some online stores price in foreign currencies (EB store: Saudi riyals only, read as two facts: Saudi riyals, and no other currency). A registered seller invoicing in a foreign currency must show the value in rials with the prevailing rate (Tax Authority, effective 2002-05-25), which names no currency area. Which currencies a market may carry is S-09's.

option: (b) Prices per market
needs: Nothing particular beyond (a): the seller sets them.
note: A price per currency area needs a market per area (S02-D4 (a), unknown).

option: (c) Prices converted by the platform at the exchange rate: a rate per currency area
needs: A published rate for each currency area.
note: Market rates: a local exchange-rate site for Aden (exrye.com), and ACAPS for Sana'a's old notes, 'Unofficial exchange rates sourced from YemenSul, Telegram'. Central-bank rates: the Sana'a bank keeps a ceiling selling price of 530.50 rials to the dollar in a daily statement on its website (2026-03-17); the Aden bank fixed 1,558 (2026-02-15; 2026-04-24), while the black market traded at 1,520 (2026-02-15). Both banks hold their rate fixed (2026-02; 2026-04-24). A quote for the currency's code from an international provider matches neither area: (e), its per-currency row.

option: (c) Prices converted by the platform at the exchange rate: the rates as a feed
needs: Those rates in a form a platform can read each day.
as_of: YE-B028: 2026-03-17; YE-E1306: 2026-10-10 (captured); unknowns.tsv's read: the capture of 2026-10-10
what_would_show_it: A source that gives each currency area's rate daily in a form a platform can read (an API or a dated bulletin), reachable from where Sharrwah runs, with its terms of use.
note: The Sana'a bank publishes its daily statement on its website, but Stage 1's capture could not read that bank's decisions and circulars pages from outside Yemen ('connection reset', unknowns.tsv, YA-88's read); ACAPS's own rates come from a Telegram channel.

option: (d) A price by the buyer's country
needs: The buyer's country: nothing particular in any market.
note: A price by currency area needs the buyer's area (S02-D4 (a), unknown).

option: (e) An exchange rate held per market, set by the seller or automatic (Shopify, for markets that hold a currency), kept on each order
needs: A rate for each market, set by the seller or taken from a source, true where that market's buyers pay; each order keeping the rate used.
note: Each currency area has its own published rate (on 8 to 10 October 2026, 533 old-note rials to the dollar in Sana'a and 1,562 in Aden; the central banks' ceiling of 530.50 and fixed 1,558); a reading: a market whose buyers are all in one area can take that area's rate. Under this option a market drawn for an area within a country inherits its parent's currency (S02-SH-104, register.tsv), so two areas of one country sharing a code can't sell at two rates: S02-D9. A rate taken automatically needs a source a platform can read ((c), its feed row: unknown). The rate moves (Q2's cases, as the next row); a reading: an order's amounts can be read later only with the rate it kept.

option: (e) An exchange rate held per currency: Salla's, at the currency's rate; Zid's automatic rate between two markets' currencies; WooCommerce's manual rate
needs: One rate per currency pair, true wherever a market of that currency sells.
note: On 8 to 10 October 2026 a dollar bought 1,562 rials in Aden's market and 533 old-note rials in Sana'a, while an international provider's mid-market quote was 236.197 (Wise), matching neither; 'two separate monetary systems and two sharply divergent exchange rates' (2026-08-07). Changing (Q2's cases): 682 in Aden and 600 in Sana'a in January 2020 (YC-286); a record low of about 2,903 for the new rial in mid-July 2025 (YC-34); 3,000 before the Aden bank's 2025 measures (YC-305); Aden's fixed rate moved from 1,617 to 1,558 (YC-86); the government's area floated the rate before fixing it (YC-89, YC-306); the international quote's all-time high was 251, in September 2017 (YC-92). The need stands: no reference sells two areas of one country under one code at two rates (register.tsv, S02-D9 (b)); S02-D9.

option: (a) Not providing for it: rules key on the country only, an area counting only where it has a country code of its own
needs: The rules that depend on where the seller is (payment services, the currency, the exchange rate) to be one per country, or each area whose answers differ to be a country of its own.
product_gap: As this decision's question, which takes up S02-D3's and S02-D2's gaps: one answer per country where a country's areas answer to different authorities for payment services, the currency and the exchange rate, and no checks on a move between such areas.
note: A reading: the records give both areas as parts of one country, with 'two YER currency areas' (YE-E1308); the rules that differ by area are S02-D3 (a)'s.

option: (b) An area within the country as a key for some rules, as the references do for tax and one feature
needs: An area within the country that the seller's address names, for the rules this option keys on it (the store's own taxes, the tax on the platform's fee, a feature's eligibility).
evidence: As S02-D4 (a), its first row; S02-D3 (a) for the sales tax.
product_gap: Under this option, as under (a), payment services, the currency and the exchange rate keep one answer per country where its areas' answers differ, since it keys only taxes and a feature on an area (register.tsv: no reference keys those on an area or runs a move's checks).
note: Governorates and districts are places an address can name (S02-D4 (a)). In the records the store's own sales tax is one per country (5 percent: S02-D3 (a)); a reading: the keys this option offers find no area difference to serve there, while the rules that differ by area, payment services, the currency and the rate, are not among them.

option: (c) The general form: any such rule keys on the country or an area within it; a change of such an area runs the move's checks
needs: The seller's area read from the business record's address, its changes recorded with their dates, and the area that served each order kept on it: nothing particular beyond an address that names the area.
evidence: As S02-D4 (a), its first row; S02-D2, its every-option row, for a move's checks.
note: Among the checks a move between areas would run: whether a payment provider from the old area may operate in the new one (Sana'a providers are not authorised in Aden without separate infrastructure in the South, 2024-04-05: S02-D2).

option: (c) The general form: the bounds of the area a rule keys on
needs: For a rule whose answer differs by an authority's area (payment services, the currency, the exchange rate), that area's bounds as places an address names.
what_would_show_it: As S02-D4 (a), its second row: a dated source listing the governorates and districts each authority holds, whether any is split between them, and how the bounds have moved.
note: The rules that differ by area, and their changes in 2024 and 2025 (YC-116, YC-117, YC-119, YC-288), are S02-D3 (a)'s. A reading: where an authority's area is the key, its bounds can change while the seller stays put; the records hold no case of that.

option: (a) Not providing for it: a currency is its code, and the rate a code's (Salla, Zid, WooCommerce)
needs: One rate per currency code, true wherever a market of that code sells.
product_gap: As this decision's question: one currency code can cover two currency areas of one country, with notes one area doesn't accept and exchange rates about three to one apart, and a currency held by its code can't tell them apart.
note: On 8 to 10 October 2026, 533 old-note rials to the dollar in Sana'a and 1,562 in Aden, and an international quote of 236.197 matching neither (S02-D7 (e), its per-currency row); the new notes are barred in the north (S02-D7 (a)).

option: (b) A rate per market (Shopify, for markets that hold a currency); a market drawn for an area within a country inherits its parent's currency
needs: A published rate for each market's currency.
product_gap: As this decision's question: this option's markets for an area within a country inherit the parent's currency, so two areas of one country sharing a code can't sell at two rates.
note: A reading: a market whose buyers are all in one currency area can take that area's rate; one spanning both has no rate true for all its buyers (S02-D7 (e)).

option: (c) A market's currency names a currency area within its code, with its own rate, held per market; each order keeps its market and rate
needs: Each currency area named, with the notes it accepts, and a rate for each, set by the seller or published.
evidence: YK-12 (YE-E1308); YA-15 (YE-E1307, YE-C048); case YC-101; the rates as S02-D7 (c), its per-area row
note: Two YER currency areas: old notes in the north, where the Sana'a bank banned the Aden bank's new notes in January 2020, and new notes in the south and east (2026-10-10); which notes an area accepts has changed (YC-101: Aden provided in 2024 for withdrawing notes printed before 2016). The rates per area are published (S02-D7 (c)); a rate taken automatically needs a source a platform can read (S02-D7 (c), its feed row: unknown).

option: (c) A market's currency names a currency area: which buyers are in which area
needs: Which buyers are in which currency area: the areas' bounds as places an address names.
note: The records name the currency areas by authority and direction ('the north', 'the south and east'), not by governorate.
